derivation.rule: Decode every retained run of the approved sanitized fixture and partition it under one candidate framing interpretation, in which consecutive candidate frames each start with a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length prefix. Record each candidate frame by offset and length, and record the 7 marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them wherever a candidate frame payload starts with the marker. The interpretation is a candidate and does not establish the prefix width. No other payload byte is copied.

candidateLengthPrefix.value: count of bytes that follow the prefix in the same candidate frame

proposedVersionPolicy.statement: Proposal only, for M1-025 to adopt or reject. If adopted, the client accepts a peer only when the 4 bytes after the marker equal 00 01 00 06 exactly, and rejects any other value with a typed error before it interprets any later frame. No version range, negotiation, downgrade or fallback is proposed, and no other version is claimed to interoperate.

limits: One observation of one external version pair on one locked host pair, re-read from the registered fixture without any new capture; it represents nothing beyond that observation.

All 11 candidate length values lie between 4 and 24, so the three high-order bytes of every candidate prefix are zero. The bytes therefore do not uniquely establish a 4-byte prefix width: a narrower 2-byte big-endian prefix also partitions all 7 runs, as alternativeReadings shows, so prefix width uniqueness stays unknown. The bytes also exercise no length value of 256 or more, no sign bit and no maximum frame length.

Under the candidate interpretation every retained run starts and ends on a candidate frame boundary. Runs 5 and 6 each carry several complete candidate frames, 4 and 2, so multiple complete candidate frames coalesced in a single retained run were observed. No candidate frame spans two retained runs, so fragmentation or split delivery was not observed and reassembly of a split frame is not exercised.
A retained run is a direction run of the captured TCP byte stream. Its boundaries are capture and read boundaries, not protocol frame boundaries in general.
Only the marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them are identified inside any frame payload. Every other payload byte stays uninterpreted and is recorded here by offset and length only.
The link between the 4 bytes after the marker and protocol version 1.6 rests only on the version the external programs reported through their own command-line metadata.
TLS was disabled for this single observation so that payload bytes were observable; the MacKVM production TLS default stays enabled, fail-closed and unvalidated by this artifact.
Windows was not executed in M1 under docs/adr/M1-SCOPE-001-linux-only-validation.md; no Windows result is recorded here.
nonClaims: No message code, message type or message name is identified in any frame.

No exact length-prefix width is established. The 4-byte unsigned big-endian reading is a candidate interpretation that rejects the 4-byte little-endian reading only, and M1-025 must not freeze an exact prefix width from this artifact until separately approved discriminating evidence exists.
No field meaning, width or order is established inside any frame payload beyond the marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them.
No general version negotiation, version range, downgrade or mismatch behavior is claimed; one version value was observed.
No compatibility is claimed between Barrier versions, between Barrier and MacKVM, or between platforms.
No Windows result and no Windows Barrier Server compatibility is claimed.
No TLS, certificate or trust behavior is observed or claimed.
No parser, encoder, Swift source or public contract is introduced; M1-025 alone freezes the wire contract.
